title: Meeting Card v1
description: One JSON per meeting reflection session. Captures the meeting's context (project link, purpose, attendees), the user's own intent before the coach speaks, the coach's high-level analysis (strengths, growth points, reflection questions), and the user's reasoning logged across the session. Companion to the project-card; lives in <project>/meetings/.

schema_version.description: Meeting-card schema version. v1 is the initial version.

id.description: Format: MTG-{customer_code}-{project_code}-{YYYY-MM-DD}-{NN}. NN is a 2-digit ordinal if multiple meetings on one date in the same project; otherwise 01. The {customer_code}-{project_code} portion must match the linked project-card id.

project_id.description: Reference to the project-card id. The project-card must exist before the meeting-card is created.

title.description: Short human-readable label, e.g., 'Vendor kickoff with Acme Cloud' or 'Steering group week 14'.

meeting_type.description: Type of meeting. Drives the coach's prior on what 'good facilitation' looks like in context.

purpose.description: Why did the group come together? 1-3 sentences. Hard non-empty (mirrors project-card.purpose mechanic — prevents empty metadata).

desired_outcome.description: What did this specific meeting need to produce or move forward? One sentence.

attendees.description: People present. When contact_id is set, the contact-card is the authoritative source; name and party here are convenience copies that may be stale.

contact_id.description: Optional reference to a contact-card. If set, name/role/party here are convenience copies of the canonical record.

role.description: Role in this meeting, e.g., 'project sponsor', 'tech lead', 'vendor PM'.

party.description: Side at the table. Aligns with project-card stakeholders[].party vocabulary.

user_role.description: The user's role in this meeting.

user_intent.description: What did YOU want to land in this meeting? Written by the user before the coach analyzes. The coach mirrors against this — without it, the coach has nothing to compare its read to and slips into reviewer-mode.

user_self_assessment.description: Optional: the user's own pre-coach read on how the meeting went. Written before the coach speaks. Sharpens the Socratic frame — the coach can ask 'you wrote X here, where in the transcript do you see that?'

transcript_provided.description: Whether the user pasted a transcript. False means coaching was conducted from memory or notes only — analysis confidence is lower and the coach must flag that explicitly.

transcript_excerpt.description: Short excerpt for identification (NOT the full transcript). Required when transcript_provided is true — see conditional rule below.

strengths.description: Specific moments where the user facilitated well. Evidence-anchored; never generic praise.

moment.description: Anchor: a quote, time marker, or section.

skill.description: The facilitation skill demonstrated, e.g., 'reframing', 'silence-holding', 'inviting dissent', 'naming the elephant'.

growth_points.description: Moments to revisit. Coach surfaces; user reasons. Capped at 3 to force selectivity — a real coach picks the few that matter, not every imperfection. Each item ends with a reflection_prompt, NEVER a prescription.

reflection_prompt.description: Open question for the user to reason with. Examples: 'What do you think was happening for X at that moment?' 'If you replayed those 30 seconds, what would you want to land differently?' NEVER 'next time you should do Y'.

reflection_questions.description: Overarching questions the coach raises about this meeting — pattern-level, not moment-level. E.g., 'Whose voice did you not hear today?' 'When you felt resistance from the sponsor, what was the assumption underneath your reply?'

pattern_read.description: Optional one-paragraph high-level read on what the coach saw as the through-line of this meeting. NOT a summary of what was said (that would be minutes) — a read on the facilitation pattern.

user_reflections.description: Append-only log of what the user reasoned to after the coach's prompts. Filled during and after the session — this is the substance the user is here to grow.

responds_to.description: Optional pointer to a growth_point or reflection_question this responds to (e.g., 'growth_points[1]'). Index-based; valid for the analysis as written. If the analysis is re-run and arrays reshuffle, this pointer is best-effort only — for durable longitudinal tracking, copy the original observation text into the reflection.

previous_meeting_card_id.description: Link to the immediately preceding meeting-card in the same project, for longitudinal tracking of recurring patterns.

status.description: analyzed = coach produced analysis (the default state). archived = closed; no further reflection expected. Whether the user has reflected is derivable from user_reflections.length > 0 — do not encode it as a status.
